questions.question: When connecting a converter dolly to a second or third trailer, the trailer height should be:

options.text: Slightly higher than the center of the fifth wheel.
Level with the center of the fifth wheel.
Slightly lower than the center of the fifth wheel.
Next to the center of the fifth wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slightly lower than the center of the fifth wheel.
questions.explanation: The trailer should be slightly lower than the center of the fifth wheel when connecting a converter dolly to a second or third trailer.

questions.question: Before driving, check that air reaches all trailers by:

options.text: Opening the rear shut-off valves and listening for escaping air.
Closing the rear shut-off valves and listening for escaping air.
Disconnecting air supply lines and listening for escaping air.
Rolling each trailer down a hill and testing the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Opening the rear shut-off valves and listening for escaping air.
questions.explanation: Open the shut-off valves on the rear of the last trailer. If air escapes from these valves, the air brake system is supplying air to the entire vehicle.

questions.question: What is another name for the service line?

options.text: Control line
Exchange line
Surplus line
Parallel line

questions.correctAnswerText: Control line
questions.explanation: The service line is also called the control line or signal line. It carries air to the trailer brakes when you press the foot brake or use the trailer hand brake.

questions.question: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS):

options.text: Allows wheels to lock up.
Prevents wheels from locking up.
Makes it easier to turn a large vehicle.
Assists with the operation of brake lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevents wheels from locking up.
questions.explanation: ABS prevents your vehicle's wheels from locking up when you brake hard.

questions.question: Having ABS on only one axle:

options.text: Does not change braking in any way.
Is not possible.
Gives the driver better control when braking.
Causes extra strain on the other axles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gives the driver better control when braking.
questions.explanation: Even if ABS is on only one axle, it gives you better control of your vehicle when braking.

questions.question: The trailer hand valve:

options.text: Should always be used for parking.
Should only be used for parking on a downhill.
Should never be used for parking.
Should only be used when transporting cargo.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should never be used for parking.
questions.explanation: Do not use the trailer hand valve for parking. This can leak all the air out of the brake system, causing the brakes to release. Use the parking brake instead.

questions.question: Rollovers happen when:

options.text: A truck driver is driving too fast.
The driver of a vehicle in front of a truck is moving too slowly.
A truck driver is driving too slowly.
ABS is working effectively.

questions.correctAnswerText: A truck driver is driving too fast.
questions.explanation: Rollovers happen when you drive too fast. To prevent rollovers, load cargo low to the ground and take turns and curves slowly.

questions.question: After connecting the air lines to the trailer while coupling, you should:

options.text: Supply air to the trailer.
Chock the wheels.
Inspect the fifth wheel.
Connect the electrical cord.

questions.correctAnswerText: Supply air to the trailer.
questions.explanation: After connecting the air lines to the trailer while coupling, supply air to the trailer.

questions.question: A combination vehicle has:

options.text: One air line.
Two air lines.
Three air lines.
Four air lines.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two air lines.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles have two air lines: a service line and an emergency line.

questions.question: If a trailer is too high:

options.text: It will not make a difference when coupling.
It may not couple correctly.
Coupling will be more secure.
Coupling will be easier.

questions.correctAnswerText: It may not couple correctly.
questions.explanation: Make sure the trailer is at the correct height before coupling. If the trailer is too high, it may not couple correctly.

questions.question: Trailers with low clearance underneath may be hard to drive:

options.text: On interstate highways.
Over railroad crossings.
On dirt roads.
At the posted speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over railroad crossings.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossings can be difficult to cross with a trailer that has low clearance. Long trailers and single-axle tractors have extra trouble crossing raised crossings.

questions.question: Combination vehicles:

options.text: Are usually shorter than single commercial vehicles.
Are usually lighter than single commercial vehicles.
Require more skill to drive than single commercial vehicles.
Are easier to drive than single commercial vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Require more skill to drive than single commercial vehicles.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles are usually heavier and longer than single commercial vehicles. This means they need more driving skill.

questions.question: What is off-tracking?

options.text: When a vehicle's front wheels follow a different path than its rear wheels
When a vehicle's wheels all follow the exact same path
When a load shifts during a turn
When a vehicle's wheels run over a curb during a turn

questions.correctAnswerText: When a vehicle's front wheels follow a different path than its rear wheels
questions.explanation: When a vehicle turns a corner, the rear wheels follow a different path than the front wheels. This is called off-tracking.

questions.question: When backing up to couple a trailer, position the tractor:

options.text: At a 90-degree angle in front of the trailer.
Directly in front of the trailer.
At a 30-degree angle in front of the trailer.
At a 60-degree angle in front of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Directly in front of the trailer.
questions.explanation: Position the tractor directly in front of the trailer. Backing at an angle could cause the trailer to move and damage the landing gear.

questions.question: When coupling a trailer:

options.text: Make sure to couple matching glad hands.
Any glad hand can be connected to any other glad hand.
It is best to leave one glad hand unattached.
Only one set of glad hands should be connected.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure to couple matching glad hands.
questions.explanation: Connect matching glad hands. They are often color-coded to prevent mistakes. Blue is used for service lines and red is used for emergency lines.

questions.question: Proper coupling technique:

options.text: Is the same on all vehicles.
Is essential to the safe operation of a vehicle.
Includes ensuring that the fifth wheel plate is not greased.
Can be learned over time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is essential to the safe operation of a vehicle.
questions.explanation: Knowing proper coupling and uncoupling is critical for safe operation of combination vehicles. Improper coupling can be very dangerous.

questions.question: After finishing a pre-trip inspection, you should:

options.text: Close the service line valve.
Remove the service line valve.
Leave the emergency line valve open.
Leave the rear shut-off valves open.

questions.correctAnswerText: Close the service line valve.
questions.explanation: Before driving, open the rear emergency and service line valves to check that air reaches all brakes. Close both valves before you start driving.

questions.question: Fully-loaded rigs:

options.text: Are less likely to roll over than empty rigs.
Are more likely to roll over than empty rigs.
Are just as likely to roll over as empty rigs.
Should not be driven.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are more likely to roll over than empty rigs.
questions.explanation: Loaded rigs have a higher center of gravity due to the cargo weight. They are 10 times more likely to roll over in a crash than empty rigs.

questions.question: Pull out the trailer air supply control to test:

options.text: The parking brake.
The trailer emergency brakes.
The trailer service brakes.
The landing gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer emergency brakes.
questions.explanation: Test the trailer emergency brakes before you start driving. After checking that the trailer rolls freely, pull out the trailer air supply control. Pull forward slightly and make sure the trailer does not move.

questions.question: A loss of air pressure in the emergency line will cause:

options.text: The service brakes to activate.
The tractor protection valve to close.
The rear trailer to detach from the combination.
The suspension springs to extend.

questions.correctAnswerText: The tractor protection valve to close.
questions.explanation: The tractor protection valve keeps air in the trailer's brake system if the trailer breaks away or develops a leak. A loss of air pressure in the emergency line will cause the tractor protection valve to open and the trailer emergency brakes to activate.
